# Verification analysis: rhel9-drift-remediation

Job: `2026-09-02__10-00-14`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> Bring the drifted RHEL 9 systems `node1` through `node4` back to the site's
> standard rsyslog configuration. Each system should accept TCP syslog on port
> 5514 and write `local0` messages to `/var/log/infraset-app.log`.
>
> Preserve the existing application data at
> `/var/lib/infraset-app/data/records.db` on every node while correcting the
> package, service, configuration, and security drift.

## Trial `rhel9-drift-remediation__RuPB8z6`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material task outcomes are satisfied on node1 through node4. Direct post-restart and final observations demonstrate healthy rsyslog package/configuration/service state, TCP 5514 acceptance with persistent security policy, functional local0 delivery, and unchanged application data. The mandatory restart protocol was successfully executed and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities, with no harmful residue observed.

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **standard_rsyslog_state — Satisfied:** Rsyslog package, configuration, and service are in the required standard state on node1 through node4.
  - **Why:** Every final audit shows an installed and unmodified rsyslog package, a syntax-valid configuration loading imtcp on port 5514 and routing local0.*, and an enabled, active service.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-61c02f135d2f46e0`, `cmd-80324509b0f54495`, `cmd-281768dd2fe744a0`, `cmd-524f5e6340774697`
- **tcp_5514_security — Satisfied:** Every node accepts TCP syslog on port 5514 with the necessary firewall and SELinux security state.
  - **Why:** All nodes have IPv4 and IPv6 wildcard rsyslog listeners on TCP 5514, active firewalld rules in both runtime and permanent configuration, SELinux enforcing with 5514 assigned to syslogd_port_t, and the destination log labeled var_log_t. Lifecycle snapshots independently confirm the final listeners.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-61c02f135d2f46e0`, `cmd-80324509b0f54495`, `cmd-281768dd2fe744a0`, `cmd-524f5e6340774697`, `global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets`, `global:after_executor:node2:listening-sockets`, `global:after_executor:node3:listening-sockets`, `global:after_executor:node4:listening-sockets`

  - **Why:** Each node accepted a unique local0.notice message over TCP through its managed IP and the same marker was directly observed in /var/log/infraset-app.log. This behavior was demonstrated after each node restart and again in the final audits.

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **1.000**. No unnecessary mutations were identified, so none require classification as retained or reverted. The atomic configuration replacements, SELinux/firewall corrections, service enable/start actions, bounded syslog test records, and scheduled node reboots all had direct remediation, validation, or mandatory restart-protocol roles. Test records remained only in the intended log as bounded evidence. Final snapshots show no failed services, damaged package state, or abnormal temporary-file residue. Restart evidence is otherwise complete on every node: healthy pre-state and boot identity, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service, listener, security, functional routing, and application data; fixed lifecycle boot identities corroborate the changes.

## Trial `rhel9-drift-remediation__cdoHfda`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material task outcomes are satisfied on node1 through node4. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: every node has a healthy pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service, security, data, and functional delivery state. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently match the executor's before/after identities.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |

| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.990 | 54/4 |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** All four nodes have an intact rsyslog package, valid standardized configuration for TCP 5514 and local0 logging, and an enabled, active service.
  - **Why:** Post-reboot checks on every node show the same installed rsyslog RPM, clean package verification, identical validated configuration, and rsyslog enabled and active.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a6f5d576b32e48ce`, `cmd-0391a5abeeef41ba`, `cmd-6241396ba5fa46b3`, `cmd-d324e8580f5241fa`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** Security drift is corrected so the required receiver operates while SELinux remains enforcing and firewalld permits TCP 5514 persistently.
  - **Why:** Every final check shows SELinux enforcing, TCP 5514 assigned to syslogd_port_t, the destination log labeled var_log_t, and active plus permanent firewall allowance. Node1's prepared tmp_t drift was directly relabeled before successful retesting.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-f7ecfd1c936e4f16`, `cmd-a6f5d576b32e48ce`, `cmd-0391a5abeeef41ba`, `cmd-6241396ba5fa46b3`, `cmd-d324e8580f5241fa`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** Each node accepts TCP syslog on port 5514 and writes local0 messages to /var/log/infraset-app.log.
  - **Why:** All four nodes directly show rsyslog listening on TCP 5514 and successful unique local0 test-message delivery to the required file after their reboots. The initial node1 failure occurred before its prepared SELinux label drift was corrected and was followed by repeated successful tests.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ad96ef9faff8468a`, `cmd-1e59957050d24b1e`, `cmd-772e5baa0abe46bb`, `cmd-af092a339dab433e`, `cmd-a6f5d576b32e48ce`, `cmd-0391a5abeeef41ba`, `cmd-6241396ba5fa46b3`, `cmd-d324e8580f5241fa`, `global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets`, `global:after_executor:node2:listening-sockets`, `global:after_executor:node3:listening-sockets`, `global:after_executor:node4:listening-sockets`
- **R4 — Satisfied:** Preserve /var/lib/infraset-app/data/records.db on every node while remediating drift.
  - **Why:** Each node's final and post-reboot SHA-256 digest exactly matches its prepared digest; the files remained present throughout the captured remediation.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ad96ef9faff8468a`, `cmd-1e59957050d24b1e`, `cmd-772e5baa0abe46bb`, `cmd-af092a339dab433e`, `cmd-a6f5d576b32e48ce`, `cmd-0391a5abeeef41ba`, `cmd-6241396ba5fa46b3`, `cmd-d324e8580f5241fa`
